tool.name: ConcaveHull

summary.para:
View online help files: https://www.jennessent.com/geometric-tools/concave-hull.html
Builds a concave hull -- the shape of a cloud of points -- by any of the three classic methods: chi (characteristic) shapes, always one simple polygon containing every point; alpha shapes, the only method that can return multiple parts and interior holes; or the k-nearest-neighbours hull. One Concavity setting (0 = the convex hull, 100 = maximum detail, blank = automatic) controls how tightly the hull follows the points; an optional case field builds one hull per group. Equivalent to the concave-hull and alpha-shape tools of PostGIS, CGAL and QGIS; Esri's closest analog (Aggregate Points) needs an Advanced license. Works at every license level.

tool.usage:
Builds the shape of a cloud of points. The convex hull -- the only hull Esri's Minimum Bounding Geometry offers -- bridges straight across every bay and gap, so for a C-shaped stand of trees, an arc of telemetry fixes or an L-shaped survey it can wildly overstate the occupied area. A concave hull follows the cloud's actual outline, with a sensitivity setting deciding how tightly.
Three methods -- the three classic lineages of the problem, genuinely different algorithms with different guarantees:
• Chi shape (characteristic shape) -- the default (Duckham, Kulik, Worboys and Galton 2008, Pattern Recognition 41:3224-3236, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.patcog.2008.03.023). Starts from the Delaunay triangulation, whose boundary is the convex hull, and repeatedly removes the longest boundary edge whenever removal keeps the shape clean. Guarantees: always one simple polygon containing every point, degrading gracefully to the convex hull, with nested shapes as the setting tightens. The best-behaved choice for most uses. • Alpha shape (Edelsbrunner, Kirkpatrick and Seidel 1983, IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 29:551-559, https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.1983.1056714). Imagine erasing the plane with a disk of a chosen radius: the alpha shape is everything the disk cannot reach without hitting a point. The only method that can return multiple disjoint polygons and interior holes -- two separate herds become two shapes, telemetry ringing a lake keeps the lake as a hole (check Allow multiple parts and interior holes; otherwise the tool picks the smallest radius that keeps the shape in one piece). • k-nearest-neighbours hull (Moreira and Santos 2007, Proc. 2nd Int. Conf. on Computer Graphics Theory and Applications (GRAPP), 61-68, https://doi.org/10.5220/0002080800610068). A gift-wrapping walk where each next boundary vertex is chosen among the current point's k nearest neighbours; smaller k hugs the points more tightly. If a walk fails to close around every point the tool raises k automatically and reports the k it used.
One Concavity setting. Set Concavity from 0 (the convex hull, all three methods) to 100 (each method's true extreme: the exactly-covering alpha; the tightest k = 3; every removable chi edge removed), or leave it blank for automatic. The automatic settings are deliberately more moderate than 100: the chi method separates gap-spanning edges from density-scale edges with a two-class threshold over its full nested family; the alpha method takes the smallest radius keeping every point covered (the "optimal alpha" rule of CGAL and PostGIS) and adds a 50% stability margin, since the exactly-covering radius tends toward spiky one-triangle isthmuses; the k-NN method uses a k that grows with the point count (about the square root of n), raised further only if the hull cannot close. Exact per-method parameters (the alpha radius and chi edge length as real distances, or k itself) live under Advanced and override Concavity.
Groups. An optional case field builds one hull per field value -- per animal, per survey period, per cluster ID -- each carrying its group value, point count, the parameter actually used, part and hole counts, and geodesic area and perimeter.
Consider the LoCoH and Kernel Density tools too. Two other tool families in this toolbox capture the shape of a point cloud, each answering a different research question. The Local Convex Hull (LoCoH) family unions many small local hulls, which not only follows the outline but also identifies areas of higher point density (utilization isopleths) -- the standard approach for home-range estimation. The Enhanced Kernel Density tools give a heat-map version of the points' shape -- a continuous density surface rather than a hard boundary -- and likewise reveal where the points concentrate, with contour and proportion companions for drawing density isopleths. If the question is "where do these points spend their weight" rather than "what outline do they occupy," reach for LoCoH or Kernel Density; this tool is the better fit for a single clean footprint polygon.
Equivalents elsewhere. These methods are the same ones behind PostGIS's ST_ConcaveHull and SFCGAL ST_AlphaShape / ST_OptimalAlphaShape, CGAL's Alpha_shape_2, and the QGIS concave-hull processing algorithms (both its k-nearest-neighbours and alpha-shape variants) -- so results can be matched across software. Esri's closest analog, Aggregate Points, requires an Advanced license; this tool runs at every license level.
Geometry notes. Layer selections are honored; duplicate points are dropped before analysis; groups with fewer than 3 distinct points are skipped with a warning. Geographic (latitude/longitude) points are solved in per-group azimuthal-equidistant working projections, and every area and perimeter is geodesic.

dialogReference.para: The point cloud to outline -- telemetry fixes, plot locations, occurrence records. A layer selection is honored; duplicate points are dropped automatically.
Chi shape (characteristic shape) -- the default: always one simple polygon containing every point, degrading gracefully to the convex hull.
Alpha shape -- the eraser-disk shape: the only method that can return multiple disjoint parts and interior holes.
k-nearest-neighbours hull -- a boundary walk among each point's k nearest neighbours; k is raised automatically if the walk cannot close.

param.name: case_field
param.displayname: Case field (optional -- one hull per value)

dialogReference.para: Optional: build one hull per value of this field -- per animal, per survey period, per cluster. Each output hull carries its group value.

param.name: concavity
param.displayname: Concavity (0 = convex hull, 100 = maximum detail; blank = automatic)

dialogReference.para: How tightly the hull follows the points: 0 gives the convex hull under every method, 100 each method's most detailed valid shape (the exactly-covering alpha; the tightest k = 3; every removable chi edge gone), and blank picks each method's more moderate automatic setting (the chi gap-versus-density threshold; the smallest valid alpha plus a 50% stability margin; a k near the square root of the point count). The exact per-method parameters under Advanced override this.

param.name: allow_parts
param.displayname: Allow multiple parts and interior holes (Alpha shape only)

dialogReference.para: Alpha shape only: allow the hull to split into several disjoint polygons (separate clusters) and to keep interior holes (a lake ringed by points). Unchecked, the tool picks the smallest alpha that keeps the shape in one piece.
The hull polygons: the case-field value (when used), Method, NPoints, the parameter actually used (Param_m in meters, or K_used), Parts, Holes, and geodesic Area_m2 and Perim_m.

Optional: the exact eraser-disk radius, in the units below. Smaller radii hug the points more tightly (and may drop outlying points from the shape); larger radii approach the convex hull. Overrides Concavity for the Alpha method.

param.name: chi_length
param.displayname: Edge length threshold (Chi shape -- overrides Concavity)

dialogReference.para: Optional: the exact chi edge-length threshold, in the units below -- boundary edges longer than this are carved away. Smaller values give more detail. Overrides Concavity for the Chi method.

param.name: k_neighbors
param.displayname: Number of neighbours k (k-NN hull -- overrides Concavity)

dialogReference.para: Optional: the exact starting k (at least 3). Smaller k hugs the points more tightly; if the walk cannot close around every point, the tool settles on the smallest workable k at or above your value and reports the k actually used. Overrides Concavity for the k-NN method.

param.name: linear_units
param.displayname: Units for the alpha radius and edge length

dialogReference.para: Meters, Kilometers, Feet or Miles. Output measure fields are always in meters.

scriptExample.title: Concave Hull example (stand-alone script)
scriptExample.para: One automatic chi-shape hull per animal, then an alpha-shape run allowing separate parts and holes.
scriptExample.code: import arcpy arcpy.ImportToolbox(r"C:\path\to\JennessEnterprisesTools.pyt") # your install path # method: "Chi shape (characteristic shape)" / "Alpha shape" / # "k-nearest-neighbours hull" arcpy.jenness.ConcaveHull( in_features=r"D:\data\telemetry.gdb\fixes", method="Chi shape (characteristic shape)", case_field="Animal_ID", out_features=r"D:\data\telemetry.gdb\fix_outlines") arcpy.jenness.ConcaveHull( in_features=r"D:\data\telemetry.gdb\fixes", method="Alpha shape", allow_parts=True, out_features=r"D:\data\telemetry.gdb\fix_alpha")
